note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 23-year-old sexually active woman with contraceptive implant presents with 3–4 days of constant, worsening lower midline (suprapubic) abdominal pain (8/10) with light pink vaginal spotting and mild nausea; advised urgent in-person assessment and same-day pregnancy test.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Constant lower abdominal pain located below the umbilicus, midline/suprapubic.
- Severity: ~8/10.
- Onset/duration: Started a few days ago; progressively worsening.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Light pink vaginal bleeding/spotting outside usual menses.
  - Slight vaginal discharge.
  - Nausea without vomiting.
  - Constipation last week (~1 week) now resolved; current bowel movements “seem OK.”
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No fever (no thermometer at home, does not feel feverish).
  - No dyspnea, no shoulder-tip pain.
  - No faintness on standing.
  - No dysuria; no strong urine odor; urinary frequency unclear (“I drink a lot,” notes not going as often as before).
  - Able to eat and drink; continuing usual activities but pain is very uncomfortable.
- Gynecologic/obstetric:
  - LMP approximately 2–3 weeks ago; last period was “normal.”
  - Sexually active; last intercourse ~4 days ago.
  - Contraception: Contraceptive implant (Implanon) in place ~1 year; menses irregular on implant.
  - No prior pregnancies; last pregnancy test ~1 month ago (not since pain began).

Past Medical History:
- Amoxicillin allergy.
- No prior surgeries reported.
- No prior pregnancies.

Medications:
- Contraceptive implant (Implanon); dose/route/frequency not documented (implant in situ).
- Other current medications: Not documented.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin (reaction not documented).

Social History:
- Occupation: School teacher.
- Lives with husband and husband’s family.
- Tobacco/alcohol use: Not documented (response unclear).
- Recreational drug use: Denies.
- Travel: Last abroad ~1 year ago.

Family History:
- Not recorded.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination findings: Not recorded (teleconsultation).

Investigations:
- None performed during this consult.
- Plan: Patient to perform a home pregnancy test today; in-person clinic evaluation to be arranged via support line for abdominal examination.

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Acute, worsening suprapubic pelvic pain with intermenstrual spotting in a sexually active woman on a contraceptive implant. Must exclude pregnancy-related causes (including ectopic). No red-flag systemic instability reported, but worsening course warrants in-person assessment.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Ectopic pregnancy: Supported by pelvic pain and spotting with no pregnancy test since symptom onset; implant reduces pregnancy risk but ectopic must be excluded. No shoulder pain/syncope/hemodynamic signs reported.
  - Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID): Lower abdominal pain with spotting and slight discharge; absence of fever does not exclude. No pelvic exam data available.
  - Functional/hemorrhagic ovarian cyst: Acute pelvic pain with spotting; implant use can be associated with functional cysts. Midline pain and non-sudden onset slightly less typical.

- Issue 1: Acute lower abdominal/pelvic pain with intermenstrual spotting; pregnancy status unknown.
  - Plan:
    - Perform home pregnancy test today; if positive, call back immediately for urgent evaluation.
    - Arrange face-to-face clinic appointment via support line for abdominal examination.
    - Safety-net: Seek earlier care if pain worsens significantly or if unable to keep fluids down (as advised).

- Issue 2: Possible gynecologic etiologies (PID vs functional ovarian cyst), pending in-person assessment.
  - Plan:
    - To be evaluated at face-to-face visit after examination and pregnancy status clarification. Further management to follow clinical findings.

- Issue 3: Recent constipation (resolved).
  - Plan:
    - No immediate intervention required; monitor.

- General plan items:
  - Continue usual hydration and activities as tolerated until seen.
  - Return/seek urgent care sooner if new concerning symptoms develop (per above safety-net).

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: No vitals; no physical exam; no objective testing documented; smoking and alcohol history unclear; allergy reaction details not recorded.  
● DDx vs transcript conflicts: None noted; DDx used to frame urgency of pregnancy test and in-person assessment.  
● Transcript quality: Several unclear/inaudible segments; some responses ambiguous (urinary frequency, smoking/alcohol).
